N3MT.title: Three knights against a lone king. Can White force mate? #shorts
N3MT.desc:
Two knights can't force mate, the king always slips away. Three knights can: here they close in and the last jump, Nb5, is checkmate.

Did you know this one?

QVPC.title: A whole queen against one pawn. Who wins? #shorts
QVPC.desc:
The c-pawn is one step from promotion and the white king is far away. After 1.Qb4+ Ka1 2.Qc3+ Kb1 3.Qb3+ Ka1 White can't take: 4.Qxc2 is stalemate. With a pawn on the c file this trick saves the game, so it's a draw.

Did you know this trick?

#chess #chessendgame #stalemate

ARBM.title: A rook and a knight trap the king in the corner. What is this mate called? #shorts
ARBM.desc:
The knight on f6 guards h7 and covers g8. The rook slides to h7: the king can't take it and can't run. It's the Arabian mate, one of the oldest mates in chess.

Did you know its name?

#chess #checkmate #chesstactics

K32N.title: Can 32 knights stand on the board without attacking each other? #shorts
K32N.desc:
Yes: put every one of them on a light square. A knight always jumps to a square of the other colour, so none of them can attack another. And 32 is the most you can fit.

Did you know this one?

#chess #chesspuzzle #chessfacts

KBNM.title: Bishop and knight against a lone king. Can White force mate? #shorts
KBNM.desc:
Yes, but only in a corner the bishop can reach. With a light-squared bishop the mate happens on a8 or h1. Here: 1.Kb6 Kb8 2.Ne7 Ka8 3.Kc7 Ka7 4.Nc8+ Ka8 5.Bf3#. From the worst start it can take up to 33 moves.

Could you do it?

OPPN.title: Same position. Black to move loses, White to move only draws. Why? #shorts
OPPN.desc:
King and pawn against king. If Black has to move, his king must step aside, the white king walks in and the pawn goes through. If White has to move, the black king stays right in front. It's called the opposition.

Did you know the opposition?

#chess #chessendgame #opposition

EPLT.title: The king is trapped by his own rooks. What is this mate called? #shorts
EPLT.desc:
Black's rooks stand on d8 and f8, on both sides of their king. The queen lands on e6 and covers d7, e7 and f7: checkmate. It's called the epaulette mate, the rooks sit on his shoulders like epaulettes.

Did you know its name?

#chess #checkmate #chesstactics

Q5DM.title: Can five queens attack every square on the board? #shorts
Q5DM.desc:
With four queens at least one square always stays safe. Five queens on the long diagonal (b2, c3, d4, f6, h8) cover all 64 squares, and in total there are 4,860 ways to do it with five.

Could you find another one?
